A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same bilateral-grid transformer research and are readable throughout. However, neither contains the referenced supplementary material or appendices. V2 explicitly points to unresolved 'Appendix ??' references for architecture, hyperparameters, and dataset details, limiting comparison of those details.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on DL3DV, LOM, and BilaRF, comparisons with competing methods, and component ablations in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction results, temporal-quality measurements, and reference-selection and self-supervision ablations in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: V2 retains the bilateral-grid transformer but adds automatic reference selection combining DINOv2 similarity and luminance quality. It also introduces a self-supervised rendering loss through a pretrained reconstruction model such as AnySplat, enabling hybrid training on paired and unpaired data. These change inference and training, beyond the CHROMA renaming.

E1.justification: V2 adds unpaired WildRGBD training data representing real object-centric, 360-degree captures with illumination and camera-processing variations. V1 trains on synthetically modified DL3DV scenes. The three evaluation datasets—DL3DV, LOM, and BilaRF—remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds 2DGS and WildGaussians across all three datasets, plus 2DGS-4DBAG and 3DGS-4DBAG on BilaRF. It removes DAVIGS and DashGS+BilaRF comparisons, and the BilaRF-specific 3DGS+BilaRF row. The four 2D correction comparators in Table 2 remain CoTF, MSEC, MSLTNet, and UEC.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from 44M to 137.84M parameters, 50K to 70K iterations, fixed 10-frame samples to 4–24 frames, and 256-pixel inputs with 16-pixel patches to 224-pixel inputs with 8-pixel patches. Evaluation replaces first-frame/manual references with automatic selection, including for UEC. V2 adds VBench temporal metrics and stops reporting uncorrected BilaRF metrics.

E4.justification: V1 Table 2 tests single versus multiple frames and uncertainty-weighted reconstruction. V2 Table 3 retains the frame-processing comparison, no longer reports the reconstruction-uncertainty ablation, and adds random/DINO/full reference-selection comparisons on LOM and a self-supervised-loss ablation on BilaRF. These test substantial new components and generalization mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for experimental results. The predicted aleatoric confidence maps are method components, not statistical uncertainty estimates for reported performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces many results: 3DGS+Ours PSNR CC changes from 29.12/26.82/25.05 to 27.28/26.25/25.60 on DL3DV/LOM/BilaRF. These use revised training and reference-selection settings, so they are not controlled performance gains or losses. Baseline values also change, including DL3DV DashGS LPIPS CC from 0.1682 to 0.1782. Additional backbone, temporal-quality, and ablation results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions for the reference score, self-supervised rendering objective, and bimodal exposure distribution. V1's explicit confidence-thresholding and initial reconstruction-loss equations are absent from the supplied v2. These are localized changes to algorithmic formulations; neither version presents theorems, formal guarantees, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the contribution from efficient harmonization for 3DGS to CHROMA as a broader reconstruction preprocessing framework. Automatic reference selection and learning from unpaired data through a pretrained 3D model become central claimed contributions, with applicability explicitly extended to 2DGS and feed-forward reconstruction.

C2.justification: V2 explains why illumination-invariant DINO similarity alone can select poorly exposed references and interprets self-supervision as bridging synthetic-to-real variation. V1 explicitly warns of a synthetic-training domain gap and degraded nighttime performance; v2 replaces that limitations discussion with claims of real-world generalization. Transient-object handling remains future work, but the applicability narrative is substantially more affirmative.

D1.justification: V2 specifies new loss weights, reference-score parameters, exposure-distribution parameters, and dataset-specific loss application, and adds a conditional future code/data-release statement. Conversely, v1's 5K training-scene count, gradient-clipping threshold, augmentation list, and explicit four-V100 setup are no longer documented. V2 refers further implementation details to unavailable 'Appendix ??' material; actual code availability is not established.

R1.justification: The central positioning against scene-specific appearance embeddings and single-image bilateral processing remains. V2 adds relevant connections to the 4DBAG extension, AnySplat, DINOv2, reference-selection research, and WildRGBD, while removing Light-A-Video and SimVS references. These extend the existing positioning around the new components.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method CHROMA and changing author/header information, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and conclusion, removes the 3DGS preliminaries, merges encoder/decoder explanations, and reorganizes the methodology around reference selection and training strategy. The separate limitations discussion is replaced by future work, and a reproducibility section is added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands to multiple reconstruction backbones and a runtime-quality plot; Figure 2 is redesigned around reference selection and downstream reconstruction; a new self-supervision diagram becomes Figure 3. The qualitative comparison is replaced and renumbered Figure 4. Tables are substantially restructured, with temporal columns added and ablations separated into Table 3, alongside a new conference layout.

improvement.justification: Automatic reference selection, direct temporal-quality measurements, and targeted component ablations improve the practical justification for the method. The unpaired-data experiment also addresses v1's acknowledged synthetic-domain concern, although Table 3 shows modest, mixed metric effects from self-supervision. These gains are tempered by removal of strong DAVIGS/BilaRF comparisons, reduced disclosure of some training details, and unresolved references to an absent appendix. The evidence supports a limited overall quality gain.
